data.design: Cold, pale storehouse interior; a sofa and piled belongings establish paths and obstacles. Pale cold timber, boarded windows and subdued belongings. Torn pallet mattresses, basin of dishes, laundry, discarded food, garbage and resale goods; rune-powered wooden console, glass display, corded handpiece. No general modern-electronics setting and no occult laboratory masquerading as the boys’ home.

description:
The old storehouse has become the youths’ messy home: sofa, pallet beds, laundry, dishes, waste and resale goods form a walkable maze. Ivo’s console game turns comic petty theft into an abrupt body-horror scene without making the boys supernatural experts.

Petty comic conflict becomes an approved early horror rupture through The Mending, then returns to a modest apology and the stolen object.

The storehouse is a small link in Team Abyss’s coastal resale network, not its headquarters. The boys take goods toward buyers at the docks.

Proposed evidence: ordinary resale parcels are stacked near the usable exit, while stolen personal keepsakes lie in an unsorted cupboard. Wrapping cloth has been cut down and reused, obscuring where a parcel came from. A shipment cannot simply be identified as stolen because it is untidy. The player first knows a particular necklace was taken; later testimony and an identifiable consignment can connect the same address to a fence. The pallets and dirty dishes remain someone’s living space after the confrontation.

data.description: Established resale route through the coast, not a newly implemented direct map exit.

sections: §§5.11, 8.1, 10.7 and 31: small-time theft and dock buyers; parcel arrangement is proposed.

name: The Old Storehouse
